title: Cap. VII: Remote cause — efficacy, blood-union, and intermediate parents
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles next denies it is fair to label the cause remote and distant: what matters here, he says, is not centuries of time but how efficacious the thing is. Placeus counters with a question: can an injustice that never lodged in me, but only in Adam who died millennia before I was, stand as equally immediate and proximate to me or my death as the injustice that clings in my inmost self and that all confess as my death's cause? Adam's sin was followed by corruption, and corruption by death; so corruption sits nearer to death than the sin confined to Adam alone. Garissoles also claims that people who derive corruption from Adam do not therefore treat Adam as remote, because blood-union with him is nearest even if personal union is not. Placeus reverses that: they do treat him as remote and distant — meaning first — as the fountain from which corruption streamed to everyone else. Distinguishing blood from person so as to call our nearest Adam-union a blood matter rather than a personal one leaves Placeus unpersuaded. Blood differs from blood and nature from nature by the same numerical (not specific) difference that divides person from person. I received my person through the chain of intermediate parents from Adam, and my nature the same way. Adam is first father, not nearest father; nothing reached me from him except through my nearest parents.
pass_b_english: "Nor is it fair," he adds, "that we should say that cause is remote and far off, because here one must look not to spaces of years and ages, but to the efficacy of the thing." What? is an injustice that did not stick in me, but in Adam alone, dead some thousands of years before I existed, a cause equally immediate and proximate to me or to my death, as that which inheres in me most inwardly and is by the confession of all the cause of my death? Did not corruption also follow Adam's sin, and death this? corruption is therefore a nearer cause of death than the sin that stuck in Adam alone. "Nor indeed," he subjoins, "do those who say corruption is derived from Adam propose Adam on that account as a remote and distant cause of that corruption — namely, because there is for us with him a most near union by reason of blood, though not by reason of person." On the contrary they propose him as a remote and distant cause of that corruption — that is, the first, from which it flowed out to all others. Therefore that blood is here distinguished from person, and that by reason of the former, not of the latter, a most near union with Adam is said to be ours — that for my part I do not understand. For my blood differs from blood, and my nature from nature, as much as person from Adam's person: the difference of each alike is numerical, not specific. And as I drew my person, so also my nature, through all my intermediate parents from Adam. For Adam is our father not nearest but first; and I have received, or could receive, nothing from him except through my nearest parents.
source_text: Neque par est, addit, ut eam causam dicamus esse remotam et longinquam, quia hic non ad annorum et saeculorum spatia, sed ad rei efficacitatem respiciendum est. Quid? an injustitia, quae in me non haesit, sed in solo Adamo, tot annorum millibus antequam essem mortuo, causa est aeque immediata ac proxima mihi vel morti meae, ac illa quae in me haeret intime, et est omnium confessione mortis meae causa? Annon etiam peccatum Adami secuta est corruptio, et hanc mors? est igitur corruptio causa propinquior mortis quam peccatum quod in solo haesit Adamo. Neque vero, subjungit, qui corruptionem ab Adamo derivari dicunt, Adamum ideo proponunt, tanquam causam remotam et distantem corruptionis illius, nimirum, quia est nobis cum eo ratione sanguinis proxima unio, etsi non ratione personae. Immo eum proponunt, tanquam causam corruptionis illius remotam et distantem, hoc est, primam, unde ad alios omnes dimanavit. Itaque quod sanguis hic a persona distinguitur, et illius, non hujus, ratione nobis esse dicitur proxima cum Adamo unio, id equidem non intelligo. Tam enim sanguis meus a sanguine, et natura mea a natura, quam persona a persona Adami differt: differentia est utriusque pariter numerica, non specifica: Et quam personam meam, tam naturam etiam meam per omnes meos intermedios parentes ab Adamo traxi. Est enim Adamus pater noster non proximus, sed primus; nihilque ab eo nisi per proximos meos parentes, accepi, aut accipere potui.
